rationale: The joint-prefix experiment executed in a clean copy (bd84c33f4fe647bc9470b0b48f324bca, completed, exit 0) with all seventeen comparisons complete and evaluated, and the witness admission chain now includes the new removal prerequisite: node 3 applied the conf-change entry carrying the joint-implicit removal and afterwards its own configuration excluded it from both halves, after which the re-add with leader 1 still unchanged left ordinary, configuration and context-free proposals pending while a never-removed member committed. This update attributes that retained interpretation, records the joint-route observation as durable knowledge with receipt indices, replaces the limitation that only a simple removal form had been executed, and notes that the executed revision's prefix prose still described a simple remove-3 change while the harness performed the joint one.

knowledge.statement: The same held-proposal effect is reached when the member's removal is expressed through joint consensus with automatic leave rather than as a simple configuration change. With a ConfChangeV2 whose transition is JointImplicit carrying remove node 3, node 3 applied one conf-change entry carrying the removal and was then excluded from both halves of its own configuration (voter false, outgoing false), and after it was re-added by a later committed change with leader 1 still unchanged, an ordinary invocation did not return inside a 1200 ms window, a configuration-change proposal did not return inside 800 ms, and an invocation with a context that never expires stayed pending through a 2000 ms window, while a never-removed member's invocation returned immediately and committed and, after a forced leader change, an invocation on node 3 returned immediately.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, reliable per-sender delivery, no ticks; the removal is a ConfChangeV2 with Transition JointImplicit and a single remove change, so raft itself proposes the entry that leaves the joint state; the re-addition is a simple ConfChange.

interpretations.rationale: Six retained executions agree, and this revision adds the joint-consensus removal form. In bd84c33f4fe647bc9470b0b48f324bca the witness admission chain is ctx (index 5), reapplied (index 4), removal (index 2) and admit (index 6), matched together: the removal event records that node 3 applied the conf-change entry carrying a JointImplicit removal (conf_change_entries 1, last_applied_index 2) and that its own configuration then excluded it from both halves (voter false, outgoing false), and the re-admission followed at index 4 with voter true and leader 1. All seventeen comparisons are complete and evaluated as holds: witness had not returned after 1201 ms (index 7), released only at the caller's deadline (index 8), payload absent (index 9); the context-free invocation was still pending after 2000 ms (index 11) with its payload uncommitted (index 12) and was admitted after the leader change (indices 33, 34); the configuration proposal did not return after 800 ms (index 14) and no node applied it (index 15); the never-removed member returned in 0 ms and committed (indices 17, 18); both retries did not return (indices 20, 25) while member proposals committed in those intervals (indices 23, 28); the post-leader-change invocation returned in 0 ms and committed (indices 31, 32). Source account: the run loop's gate variable is assigned only at node.go:374 (leader observed), 377 (no leader) and 426 (local member removed) and used as the receive case at node.go:386; the guard fires when applying a conf change leaves the local node without a Progress entry, which joint consensus with automatic leave also does once the joint state is left. Controls exclude cluster-wide stalls and a broken state machine, and the context-free case shows the held request is admitted and committed only after leadership changes.

knowledge.assertion: propc is armed only on observed leader change and is left nil after a re-admission
the caller sends on n.propc and stays pending while the run loop's gate variable is disarmed; a later observed leader change admits the pending request
the raft state machine returns ErrProposalDropped for a removed leader instead of blocking
intended blocking is scoped to the unknown-leader case and acceptance is expected once a leader is known; re-addition is untested
a configuration change proposed through the re-added voter was held pending and was not applied by any node
a joint-consensus removal with automatic leave leads to the same held-proposal effect after the member is re-added

counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the gate as improvised ('propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs'); this explains the dependence on leader changes but is neither a calling restriction nor a protection, and no other re-arm path exists in the snapshot.

node_test.go:352-385 shows that not returning is intended for a node that does not know the current leader. That expectation does not cover the witnessed case, and the same test expects acceptance once a leader is known.

No request is lost: held invocations are admitted unmodified once the gate is re-armed (indices 33, 34), so the harm is an unbounded wait without an error signal rather than data loss or a protocol safety violation.
The same runs contain successful paths (indices 17, 18, 23, 28, 32), showing proposals are neither generally dropped nor generally blocked.
limitations: Comparison outcomes for the earliest receipt were 'unknown' because that harness gave the three operations' result events the same names; its decisive events are complete and match the successor receipts, which have complete holds.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in this snapshot; RawNode.Propose and RawNode.ProposeConfChange have no such gate. No ticks were delivered and delivery was reliable, so no timing or network-fault characterization is claimed.

Two removal forms were executed (simple ConfChange and joint-implicit with automatic leave). Transitions that keep the member in a half of the configuration were not executed; the guard reads the local Progress entry, so they are expected not to disarm the gate, but that expectation is source-derived only.

The executed revision's prefix prose still described a simple remove-3 ConfChange while the fixed harness performed the joint-implicit removal; the harness artifact and this record describe the executed behaviour, and the prose is corrected in the successor record.

The configuration-proposal case was executed once with a single proposal (add node 9) and a single window; it establishes that the administrative entry point is affected, not a distribution over configuration-change kinds.
interpretations.joint_history: Six receipts from one fixed scenario lineage: 3592ccaf01864f56aaf06d54a3f97423-experiment (43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad), 48ce57b251a644edaaf9d17731df0b25-experiment (a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f), baee4030bf1e4f229c46ece8d0ddc365-experiment (87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4), de0272862d1842d2af26e89d955ed098-experiment (905d729b2a284c93bbbedd3c3a307ca8), 5d5aaf795784463ea4d615854bbee98a-experiment (6e187216178a49d4ae02bd8c2afaeaf9) and 6b5eedab76ea4fa7804929359921df36-experiment (bd84c33f4fe647bc9470b0b48f324bca), each registered with previous_id and a revision_reason. All six build the same configuration {1,2,3} from the same storage ConfState, elect leader 1 at term 1, remove node 3 by committed configuration change (simple in the first five, joint-implicit in the sixth), re-add it, and force the same campaign of node 2 into term 2, with the same invocation cases, deadlines, windows and operation ids. Witnesses agree field for field (witness 7/8/9 in all six; context-free 11/12; configuration proposal 14/15; control 17/18; retry 20/25; progress commits 23/28; repair 31/32), so the effect is a property of the scenario rather than of one run or one removal form.
